mixed_sign_physicality_ceiling.note: STRUCTURAL BOUND (not a fit): for pn=±1 the sign pattern's most-negative eigenvalue forces det(I+g·S) ≤ 0 once per-pair magnitude g ≥ 1/|μ_min|. The naive bond factor z EXCEEDS this ceiling ⇒ pn=±1 unphysical at z. The [1⁴] framing must supply a REDUCED (or non-uniform) per-pair magnitude below the ceiling — a sharper open than the sign alone.

result.verdict: The pp/nn signs are DERIVED (+1/−1) from the framework's own crossing convention; only the pn sign is open. Enumerating w_pn∈{−1,0,+1} at the derived magnitude z: pn=±1 give det<0 (UNPHYSICAL — the mixed-sign pattern over-rotates at magnitude z), pn=0 (the chain convention) gives 2.40 MeV (0.26×) AND decouples the pn pairs (block-diagonal — physically excluded for the pn-dominated shell). So NO discrete pn sign closes at magnitude z. The sharper finding: the sign pattern's most-negative eigenvalue caps the physical per-pair magnitude at g_ceiling < z, so the [1⁴] framing must supply a mixed sign (pn=±1) AND a reduced/non-uniform per-pair magnitude below the ceiling — NOT the naive bond factor z. No magnitude is solved-for to hit 9.243 (that would be a fit, Rule-14, refused); only the structural ceiling (an eigenvalue of the read-off sign pattern) is reported. Fixing sign+magnitude needs the explicit [1⁴] link diagram (open; candidate source #3407 Reeb Lk_R^{(k)}, still a stub).
